base: exact e470268ff446ec56728215a987ed166d5ed8fb64 plus terminal-tcg-x87-v1.patch; three files independently matched frozen built-source-v1.zip

first_difference.same_semantics: ELF disassembly and guest bytes both contain FNINIT; FLDCW 037e; FLDZ; FLDZ; DE F9; non-waiting FNSTENV; FNINIT. Hardware REX/default address encoding and pointer values differ; reserved words are deliberately not compared. AT&T objdump mnemonic direction spelling is not used as identity; DE F9 bytes are the same. Guest trace entries contain the FLDZ/FLDZ/DE F9/FNSTENV PCs 100143/100145/100147/100149. No intervening waiting x87 instruction occurs before sampling.
first_difference.cause: Old helper writes the SoftFloat invalid result to physical ST7, then translator emits an unconditional fpop. Hardware keeps both zero operands nonempty and TOP6 for unmasked #I. FNSTENV pre-mask images show the mismatch; it is not an exit-code or FXSAVE formatting discrepancy.

implemented_scope: Only register-operand FDIV/FDIVR/FDIVP/FDIVRP (D8 F0-FF, DC F0-FF, DE F0-FF) dispatch to the new helper. Both source values are sampled before any destination assignment; pop is owned by that helper.

Stack-underflow precondition sets IE/SF and clears C1. Masked stack invalid writes the default x87 indefinite to the destination and performs the requested pop; unmasked stack invalid leaves destination/tags/TOP unchanged.

Normal register division computes a local SoftFloat result and retains only current-instruction flags for the commit decision. Prior sticky SoftFloat flags are merged afterwards rather than mistaken for a new exception.

Exception precedence: invalid dominates; a quiet NaN result suppresses lower conditions; zero-divide dominates denormal; unmasked denormal suppresses lower post-computation flags. True and pseudo-denormal raw register encodings are considered.

Unmasked #I/#Z/#D updates exception flags/summary but returns without result/tag/TOP writes. Masked preconditions commit the result and requested pop. The surrounding translator still updates FIP/FOP, leaving the faulting instruction provenance available to FNSTENV and the deferred handler.
No whole-CPU backup/rollback or generic abort-on-ES was added. The existing memory-source helpers and all non-division arithmetic dispatch remain unchanged.
explicit_limits: This patch does not implement correct unmasked numeric overflow/underflow result scaling or all inexact/C1 rounding behavior; these post-computation cases are not suppressed by the pre-computation rule and remain unqualified.

Memory-source FDIV/FIDIV/FDIVR/FIDIVR conversion, operand-load faults and exception suppression are outside this patch. Memory conversions can raise flags before the old divide helper, and need a separate instruction-level design.
Other x87 arithmetic/comparison/store/pop helpers remain unchanged. Existing transcendental helper_fdiv users are not redirected.

Complete CR0.NE=0 FERR/IGNNE behavior, legacy CPU model differences, all special-value combinations and unsupported instruction priorities are not certified. The observed single division plus non-waiting FNSTENV discrepancy is independent of delayed #MF delivery.
Neither whole CPU restore nor machine state, devices/RAM/resources, Windows/WOW64 or original game correctness follows. full57 and Windows admission remain false.
